title: Outside-in Org Data Model
description: JSON Schema for Outside-in Org model files (.oio.yaml). The structural core validates users, needs, capabilities, technical systems, teams and their relationships. The optional investigation extension (OIO 1.1) adds signals, constraints, outcomes, flow decision records, metrics and embedded check-ins, so that observation, provenance and decision context survive interchange instead of being flattened into descriptions.

system.title: System
system.description: Top-level boundary descriptor. Identifies the scope of what is being modeled.

users.title: Users
users.description: People or external systems that have needs (e.g., Merchant, Eater, Operator). Each user represents a meaningfully different type with different goals.

needs.title: Needs
needs.description: What each user is trying to accomplish. Needs bridge users to capabilities.

capabilities.title: Capabilities
capabilities.description: What the system must be able to do. Capabilities are the core of an outside-in model — they represent durable system abilities, not services, technical systems or teams.

technical_systems.title: Technical Systems
technical_systems.description: Concrete implementations that enable capabilities. Technical systems declare which capabilities they implement and which external systems they depend on.

teams.title: Teams
teams.description: Organizational units that steward capabilities and technical systems. Classified using the Team Topologies pattern language.

org_groups.title: Organisational Groups
org_groups.description: Optional grouping of teams into larger organizational units (value streams, platforms, tribes, domains, org-units).

data_assets.title: Data Assets
data_assets.description: Shared storage and messaging infrastructure. Model data assets when multiple technical systems share the same database, cache, or event stream — this reveals implicit coupling.

external_dependencies.title: External Dependencies
external_dependencies.description: Systems outside the modeled boundary. Define them here; edges showing which technical systems use them come from technicalSystem.externalDeps.

metrics.title: Metrics
metrics.description: OIO 1.1. Metric definitions referenced by outcome measures, decision metrics and check-in readings. Defining a metric does not require that any reading exists.

signals.title: Signals
signals.description: OIO 1.1. Observations or reports that warrant attention. A signal is evidence that something was noticed — it is not, on its own, proof of a causal explanation or of an organisational defect.

constraints.title: Constraints
constraints.description: OIO 1.1. Conditions that limit the available choices or the ability to act. Certainty (is it assumed or confirmed?) is recorded separately from standing (does it still apply?).

outcomes.title: Outcomes
outcomes.description: OIO 1.1. Desired changes in conditions for identifiable beneficiaries. An outcome is not a user need, a capability, a delivered artefact, a milestone, or a decision's review verdict.

flow_decision_records.title: Flow Decision Records
flow_decision_records.description: OIO 1.1. Decisions being considered or made: the question, the evidence cited, the constraints in force, the options weighed, the reasoning, and any later review.

allOf.$comment: A document that carries any investigation section must declare the OIO version it was written against, so a consumer can decide whether it can read the document before it starts reading it.

entityId.title: Entity Identifier
entityId.description: A stable identifier, unique across every identified thing in the document. Identifiers do not change when a name or label is edited, which is what allows evidence and decisions to stay attached through a rename.

idRef.title: Identifier Reference
idRef.description: A reference to another record by its id. Identifiers are unique across the whole document, so a reference never needs a type to disambiguate it — an unresolvable or duplicated id is an error, never a best guess.

date.title: Date
date.description: A calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) or a full ISO 8601 timestamp.

approximateDate.title: Approximate Date
approximateDate.description: A date known only as precisely as it is known: a year (YYYY), a month (YYYY-MM), a day (YYYY-MM-DD), or a full ISO 8601 timestamp. Use the shortest form that is actually true rather than padding an unknown day to the first of the month.

entityTypeName.title: Entity Type
entityTypeName.description: The name of an OIO entity type, in the singular form of its section key.

provenance.title: Provenance
provenance.description: Where a record came from. Every field is optional: an unknown source or date is recorded by leaving the field out, never by inventing a plausible one.

source.title: Source
source.description: Who or what this came from — a role, a document, a system. Use the level of attribution that was actually agreed; a role is often the right level where a named individual is not.

source_type.title: Source Type
source_type.description: The kind of source this came from, which is what makes an evidence status interpretable.

recorded_at.title: Recorded At
recorded_at.description: When this was written down or reported. Distinct from when the underlying thing happened.

recorded_by.title: Recorded By
recorded_by.description: Who wrote this record. Distinct from `source`, which is who the claim came from.

note.title: Provenance Note
note.description: Anything about how this was collected that changes how it should be read.

reference.title: Reference
reference.description: A typed reference from an investigation record to another record in the document, by id.

target.title: Target
target.description: The id of the referenced record.

entity_type.title: Expected Entity Type
entity_type.description: Optional assertion about what kind of record the target is. When present it is checked against the resolved target, which turns a stale reference into an error rather than a silent retarget.

note.title: Note
note.description: Why this record is relevant to the referenced thing.

reading.title: Reading
reading.description: A quantitative observation of a defined metric at a point in time.

metric.title: Metric
metric.description: The id of the metric definition this reading is of.

value.title: Value
value.description: The observed value, in the unit declared on the metric definition.

context.title: Context
context.description: What was true about the measurement that a later reader would need in order to compare it fairly — the population, the window, the sampling method.

note.title: Note
note.description: A short remark about this reading.

checkIn.title: Check-in
checkIn.description: A dated observation about an outcome or a decision, recorded where it belongs rather than as a separate graph node. A check-in may be entirely qualitative: readings are optional and no measurement need be invented to record one. Observation (`note`), interpretation (`interpretation`) and a decision's review verdict (flow_decision_record.verdict) are three different things and are kept apart.

id.title: Check-in Id
id.description: Identifier for this check-in, unique across the document.

note.title: Observation
note.description: What was seen, heard or reported. This is the observation, not what anyone concluded from it.

interpretation.title: Interpretation
interpretation.description: What the recorder took the observation to mean, kept separate from the observation itself so a later reader can disagree with the reading of the evidence without losing the evidence.

readings.title: Readings
readings.description: Quantitative observations taken at this check-in. Optional and often empty.

measure.title: Measure
measure.description: A metric applied to an outcome, optionally with a baseline and a target. An outcome is representable before any of these numbers are known: a measure may name a metric and nothing else.

metric.title: Metric
metric.description: The id of the metric definition being applied.

baseline.title: Baseline
baseline.description: Where this metric stood before the change was attempted, when that is known.

target.title: Target
target.description: Where this metric is intended to reach, when a target has actually been agreed. Omit it rather than inventing one.

note.title: Note
note.description: How this metric relates to the outcome, or what it does not capture.

measurePoint.title: Measure Point
measurePoint.description: A value for a metric, with the date it applies to where known.

value.title: Value
value.description: The value, in the unit declared on the metric definition.

at.title: At
at.description: The date this value was measured (for a baseline) or is intended for (for a target).

note.title: Note
note.description: A qualitative statement of the baseline or target where no number is available.

name.title: System Name
name.description: The name of the system being modeled. Unique identifier for this model.

description.title: System Description
description.description: A description of the system scope and purpose.

version.title: Version
version.description: User-controlled version identifier for this model's content. Set automatically by the platform on export. This is not the OIO schema version — see oio_version.

oio_version.title: OIO Version
oio_version.description: OIO 1.1. The OIO schema version this document is written against. Required whenever the document carries any investigation section, so that a consumer can report what it cannot read rather than silently dropping it. A document that omits this field is a structural 1.0 document.

lastModified.title: Last Modified
lastModified.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last export. Set automatically by the serializer.

author.title: Author
author.description: Who last exported or modified this model.

user.title: User
user.description: A person or external system that has needs (e.g., Merchant, Eater, Operator).

id.title: User Id
id.description: OIO 1.1. Stable identifier. Required only if an investigation record references this user.

name.title: User Name
name.description: The name of the user. Must be unique within the model and match references from needs.

type.title: User Type
type.description: Optional free-form label expressing what kind of user this is (e.g., User, Customer, Operator, Persona, System). No fixed vocabulary — different organisations use different terms.

description.title: User Description
description.description: A description of this user — who they are and their relationship to the system.

need.title: Need
need.description: What a user (or multiple users) is trying to accomplish. Needs bridge users to capabilities.

id.title: Need Id
id.description: OIO 1.1. Stable identifier. Required only if an investigation record references this need.

name.title: Need Name
name.description: The name of the need. Must be unique within the model.

user.title: User
user.description: The user or users who have this need. Can be a single user name or a list of user names.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.description: First-person statement of what success looks like for this user. This is a sentence, not a reference: it keeps exactly the meaning it had in OIO 1.0 and is never an id of an entry in the `outcomes` section.

fulfilledBy.title: Fulfilled By
fulfilledBy.description: Capabilities that fulfil this need. Each entry is either a capability name (short form) or a relationship object (long form).

decomposesInto.title: Decomposes Into
decomposesInto.description: Sub-needs that decompose this need. Each entry is either a need name (short form) or a relationship object (long form).

capability.title: Capability
capability.description: What the system must be able to do. Capabilities are durable system abilities, not services, technical systems or teams.

id.title: Capability Id
id.description: OIO 1.1. Stable identifier. Required only if an investigation record references this capability.

name.title: Capability Name
name.description: The name of the capability. Must be unique within the model.

description.title: Capability Description
description.description: A description of what this capability provides.

visibility.title: Visibility
visibility.description: The value chain layer this capability belongs to. user-facing: directly experienced by end users; domain: core business processing; foundational: internal capabilities underpinning domain logic; infrastructure: deep infrastructure.

evolution_stage.title: Evolution Stage
evolution_stage.description: How evolved this capability is as a practice in the wider world, in the Wardley sense: genesis: novel and uncertain; custom-built: built to fit, still changing; product: a well-understood product or rental market exists; commodity: standardised and utility-like. This axis describes ubiquity and certainty of the practice. It says nothing about how well this organisation performs the capability, how mature its implementation is, or whether it is being retired.

strategic_importance.title: Strategic Importance
strategic_importance.description: The strategic importance of this capability to the business. core: essential to the core value proposition; supporting: contributes to competitive differentiation; generic: necessary but not a key differentiator.

dependsOn.title: Depends On
dependsOn.description: Other capabilities this capability requires. Each entry is either a capability name (short form) or a relationship object (long form).

decomposesInto.title: Decomposes Into
decomposesInto.description: Sub-capabilities that decompose this capability. Each entry is either a capability name (short form) or a relationship object (long form).

technicalSystem.title: Technical System
technicalSystem.description: A concrete implementation that realizes one or more capabilities. Stewardship is declared from the team side via team.stewards.

id.title: Technical System Id
id.description: OIO 1.1. Stable identifier. Required only if an investigation record references this technical system.

name.title: Technical System Name
name.description: The name of the technical system. Must be unique within the model.

description.title: Technical System Description
description.description: A description of what this technical system does.

enables.title: Enables
enables.description: Capabilities this technical system implements. Source of truth for enablement (capabilities do NOT declare enabledBy). Each entry is a capability name or a relationship object with role and description.

constrains.title: Constrains
constrains.description: Capabilities this technical system constrains. Source of truth for constraint (capabilities do NOT declare constrainedBy). Each entry is a capability name or a relationship object with role and description. This is a structural statement about an implementation limiting a capability, and is not the same thing as an entry in the `constraints` section.

dependsOn.title: Depends On
dependsOn.description: Other technical systems this technical system calls. Each entry is a technical system name or a relationship object.

externalDeps.title: External Dependencies
externalDeps.description: Names of external systems this technical system depends on. Must match entries in external_dependencies.

team.title: Team
team.description: An organizational unit that stewards capabilities and technical systems. Classified using the Team Topologies pattern language.

id.title: Team Id
id.description: OIO 1.1. Stable identifier. Required only if an investigation record references this team.

name.title: Team Name
name.description: The name of the team. Must be unique within the model.

type.title: Team Type
type.description: The Team Topologies classification. stream-aligned: aligned to a flow of work from a segment of the business domain; platform: enables stream-aligned teams to deliver with substantial autonomy; enabling: helps other teams adopt and acquire capabilities; complicated-subsystem: requires specialized knowledge.

subtype.title: Subtype
subtype.description: If type is 'undefined', use this field to specify what kind of team this is (e.g., project team, frontend team, backend team, working group, tiger team).

description.title: Team Description
description.description: A description of the team — their mission and scope.

size_band.title: Size Band
size_band.description: Number of people on the team. Defaults to 5-9 if not set. Team Topologies recommends 5–9 people per team.

stewards.title: Stewards
stewards.description: Capabilities and technical systems stewarded by this team. Each entry is a capability or technical system name, or a relationship object.

interacts.title: Interacts
interacts.description: Inline interaction declarations — how this team works with other teams.

teamInteraction.title: Team Interaction
teamInteraction.description: Declares how this team works with another team.

id.title: Interaction Id
id.description: OIO 1.1. Stable identifier for this interaction. Required only if an investigation record references it — a signal about a strained interaction points here rather than at either team.

with.title: Target Team
with.description: The name of the other team this team interacts with.

mode.title: Interaction Mode
mode.description: How the two teams work together. x-as-a-service: one team provides a service or API for the other; collaboration: two teams work closely together; facilitating: one team helps the other adopt a capability. Undefined interactions are those that do not fit with the core Team Topologies interaction modes — these are valid but should be used intentionally to highlight awkward interactions that may require special attention.

classification.title: Interaction Classification
classification.description: Classify this interaction to clarify its nature and implications. handover: work is passed from one team to another; temporal-coupling: teams must coordinate closely in time but can work asynchronously; ongoing-coordination: teams must coordinate closely and frequently; ongoing-facilitation: one team actively helps the other adopt a capability; ongoing-collaboration: two teams work closely together on an ongoing basis.

purpose.title: Interaction Purpose
purpose.description: The primary purpose of this interaction. information-sharing: exchanging information or updates; coordination: coordinating work or schedules; support: providing help or expertise; decision-making: making joint decisions; innovation: collaborating on new ideas or improvements.

duration.title: Interaction Duration
duration.description: The typical duration of this interaction. short-term: one-off or infrequent interactions; medium-term: regular interactions that last a few weeks or months; long-term: ongoing interactions that last more than a few months.

coupling_strength.title: Coupling Strength
coupling_strength.description: The strength of the coupling relationship between these teams. loose: occasional interactions with minimal coordination; moderate: regular interactions with some coordination; tight: frequent interactions with close coordination and collaboration.

health.title: Interaction Health
health.description: The health of this interaction. neutral: no view recorded; healthy: interactions are smooth and effective; problematic: interactions have some friction or issues that need attention; unhealthy: interactions are dysfunctional and causing problems.

via.title: Via
via.description: A capability or technical system involved in this interaction.

description.title: Description
description.description: Human-readable label describing the nature of this interaction.

reviewHorizon.title: Review Horizon
reviewHorizon.description: When should we review this interaction? The date at which this interaction should be reviewed for continued relevance and health. Set automatically by the platform based on the interaction mode and duration, but can be overridden by the user.

id.title: Group Id
id.description: OIO 1.1. Stable identifier. Required only if an investigation record references this group.

name.title: Group Name
name.description: The name of the grouping. Must be unique within the model.

type.title: Group Type
type.description: The type of grouping. value-stream: end-to-end flow of work delivering value to customers; platform: provides internal services used by other teams; tribe/domain: collection of teams working in the same business domain; org-unit: any other kind of organizational grouping.

size_band.title: Size Band
size_band.description: Number of people in the group.

description.title: Group Description
description.description: A description of what this group provides and what it classifies.

contains.title: Contains
contains.description: Names of the teams or capabilities contained within this group.

externalDependency.title: External Dependency
externalDependency.description: A system outside the modeled boundary. Define it here as a declaration; technical systems declare their use via technicalSystem.externalDeps.

id.title: External Dependency Id
id.description: OIO 1.1. Stable identifier. Required only if an investigation record references this dependency.

name.title: External Dependency Name
name.description: The name of the external system. Must be unique within the model and match references in technicalSystem.externalDeps.

description.title: External Dependency Description
description.description: A description of what this external system provides.

dataAsset.title: Data Asset
dataAsset.description: A shared storage or messaging resource used by one or more technical systems. Declaring data assets reveals implicit coupling between systems that share the same database, cache, or event stream.

id.title: Data Asset Id
id.description: OIO 1.1. Stable identifier. Required only if an investigation record references this data asset.

name.title: Data Asset Name
name.description: The name of the data asset. Must be unique within the model.

type.title: Data Asset Type
type.description: The kind of data asset. database: relational or document store; cache: in-memory key-value store; event-stream: Kafka or similar messaging; blob-storage: object/file storage; search-index: Elasticsearch or similar.

description.title: Data Asset Description
description.description: A description of what data this asset stores or streams.

usedBy.title: Used By
usedBy.description: Names of technical systems that use this data asset. Source of truth for data asset usage — technical systems do NOT declare which data assets they use.

relationship.title: Relationship
relationship.description: A directed relationship reference. Supports two forms: a plain string (short form — just the name) or an object with target, description, and optional role (long form). Both forms can be mixed in the same list.

oneOf.description: Short form: the name of the referenced entity.

id.title: Relationship Id
id.description: OIO 1.1. Stable identifier for this edge. Declare one only when an investigation record needs to point at the edge itself rather than at either endpoint — for example a signal about one particular dependency.

target.title: Target
target.description: The name of the referenced entity.

description.title: Description
description.description: An optional human-readable edge label describing the nature of this relationship.

role.title: Role
role.description: The role of this relationship. primary: main implementation or dependency; supporting: contributes but doesn't own; consuming: uses as a client. This says what part the relationship plays structurally. It is not a confidence level and must never be used to record how sure anyone is that the relationship exists.

metricDefinition.title: Metric Definition
metricDefinition.description: OIO 1.1. A named, reusable measure. Defining it commits nobody to a target.

unit.title: Unit
unit.description: The unit readings are expressed in (e.g. days, percent, count).

direction.title: Direction
direction.description: Which way is better for this metric.

description.title: Metric Description
description.description: How this metric is defined and gathered.

signal.title: Signal
signal.description: OIO 1.1. An observation or report that warrants attention. Three independent axes are recorded separately and must not be collapsed: signal_type says what kind of tension this is, severity says how much attention it warrants, and evidence says how well supported the claim is. A reported concern can be severe and still be uncorroborated.

name.title: Signal Name
name.description: A short statement of what was observed or reported.

description.title: Signal Description
description.description: What was observed or reported, in the words of the source where possible. Keep interpretation out of this field.

signal_type.title: Signal Type
signal_type.description: The nature of the tension. Shared vocabulary with Fast Flow Toolkit. dependency: waiting on another party; cognitive-load: more to hold than a team can carry; ownership-gap: nobody owns this; unmet-need: a user need is not being met; structural-tension: the structure itself pulls against the work; other: none of these.

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: How much attention this warrants. Shared vocabulary with Fast Flow Toolkit. This is about consequence, not about how well evidenced the claim is — see `evidence`.

evidence.title: Evidence Status
evidence.description: How well supported this claim is, given its source. These are distinct epistemic states, not a ranked scale: reported: one source said so and it has not been checked; corroborated: independent sources agree; direct-observation: the recorder saw it themselves; measured: a quantitative reading or artefact supports it; disputed: another source contradicts it. Omit the field when the standing of the evidence is genuinely unknown. Converting a report into a finding is an act someone must perform — it never happens as a side effect of import.

observed_at.title: Observed At
observed_at.description: When the underlying thing happened, as precisely as that is known. Distinct from provenance.recorded_at, which is when it was reported.

observation_window.title: Observation Window
observation_window.description: The period the observation covers, where it describes a pattern over time rather than a moment.

references.title: References
references.description: The structural entities, team interactions or declared relationships this signal is about. Referencing an entity does not assert that the entity is at fault.

reveals.title: Reveals
reveals.description: Constraints this signal bears on, and what it does to them. Encountering a signal does not on its own change a constraint's certainty: that is a separate judgement recorded on the constraint.

impedes.title: Impedes
impedes.description: Flow decision records whose enactment this signal describes an obstruction to. An impediment is an observation about a decision, not a kind of entity and not a kind of signal — the same signal keeps its signal_type and can be cited as evidence elsewhere.

supersedes.title: Supersedes
supersedes.description: A signal this one replaces. The superseded signal stays in the document; supersession records that a later reading exists, it does not delete the earlier one.

addressed_at.title: Addressed At
addressed_at.description: When this signal was considered addressed.

dismiss_reason.title: Dismiss Reason
dismiss_reason.description: Why this signal was dismissed. Shared vocabulary with Fast Flow Toolkit.

revealsLink.title: Reveals Link
revealsLink.description: What a signal says about a constraint. The verb a reader sees comes from `effect`, not from the link's name.

target.title: Constraint
target.description: The id of the constraint this signal bears on.

effect.title: Effect
effect.description: revealed: this signal is why the constraint was suspected at all; confirmed: it supports the constraint; contradicted: it tells against the constraint.

note.title: Note
note.description: How this signal bears on the constraint.

impedesLink.title: Impedes Link
impedesLink.description: An obstruction to enacting a decision, observed while enacting it.

target.title: Flow Decision Record
target.description: The id of the decision whose enactment was obstructed.

constraint.title: Constraint
constraint.description: OIO 1.1. A condition that limits the available choices or the ability to act. Certainty and standing are independent: a constraint can be confirmed and lifted, or assumed and live. A constraint is a persisting condition; a single obstruction met while enacting a decision is a signal that impedes it, and may or may not reveal a constraint behind it.

statement.title: Statement
statement.description: The condition, stated as what it prevents or requires.

description.title: Constraint Description
description.description: What is known about this condition and how it bites.

certainty.title: Certainty
certainty.description: Whether anyone has actually checked. Shared vocabulary with Fast Flow Toolkit. assumed: believed to hold, not verified; confirmed: verified with someone in a position to know. A suspected explanation for a signal is `assumed` until it is checked.

standing.title: Standing
standing.description: Whether it still bites. Shared vocabulary with Fast Flow Toolkit. live: currently limiting choices; accepted: acknowledged and worked within; lifted: no longer applies. Standing changes over time and changing it never rewrites what a past decision was made under — see constraint.bounds[].state_at_commit.

help_needed_from.title: Help Needed From
help_needed_from.description: Who would have to act for this condition to change.

bounds.title: Bounds
bounds.description: The decisions and outcomes this condition limits. Bounding a decision claims the condition materially shaped the intervention space that was open. Bounding an outcome claims it limits the condition being pursued, or the terms on which it can be pursued. Neither means 'is related to' — if the only defensible statement is that the two are connected, record no link.

references.title: References
references.description: Structural entities this condition is about.

supersedes.title: Supersedes
supersedes.description: A constraint this one replaces, for example a vaguer earlier statement of the same condition. The superseded constraint stays in the document.

boundsLink.title: Bounds Link
boundsLink.description: A constraint limiting a decision or an outcome.

target.title: Target
target.description: The id of the flow decision record or outcome this condition bounds.

state_at_commit.title: State At Commit
state_at_commit.description: The constraint's certainty at the moment the decision it bounds was committed. This is the historical record and is deliberately allowed to disagree with the constraint's current certainty: a condition later confirmed, or later lifted, does not retroactively change what the decision was taken under. Its absence on a committed decision is itself a fact — it means the condition was named after the decision was made — and must never be filled in from the constraint's present certainty. Meaningful only where the target is a flow decision record that has actually committed: a decision still in draft has no moment of commitment, so there is no belief-at-commitment to record.

note.title: Note
note.description: How this condition limited the decision or outcome.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.description: OIO 1.1. A desired change in conditions for identifiable beneficiaries. An outcome is not a user need (which is what a user is trying to accomplish, and is already true of them), not a capability, not a delivered artefact, not a project milestone, and not a decision's review verdict. An outcome is representable before any measure, target or date is agreed.

name.title: Outcome Name
name.description: The change in conditions being sought, stated as a condition rather than as an activity.

description.title: Intent
description.description: What is intended to become true, for whom, and why it matters.

status.title: Status
status.description: Where this outcome stands as a matter of pursuit. Shared vocabulary with Fast Flow Toolkit. draft: proposed, not adopted; active: being shaped; observing: a bet is placed and is being watched; achieved: the change has happened; archived: no longer pursued.

beneficiaries.title: Beneficiaries
beneficiaries.description: Who is meant to be better off. References users, teams or organisational groups. An outcome with no identifiable beneficiary is usually an activity in disguise.

references.title: References
references.description: Other structural entities this outcome concerns.

success_criteria.title: Success Criteria
success_criteria.description: How anyone would know this had happened, stated in plain language. Qualitative criteria are first-class: no number is required and none should be invented.

measures.title: Measures
measures.description: Metrics applied to this outcome, with baselines and targets where they are actually known.

target_date.title: Target Date
target_date.description: When this change is intended to have happened, if a date has been agreed.

next_review_at.title: Next Review At
next_review_at.description: When this outcome is next due to be looked at.

activated_at.title: Activated At
activated_at.description: When this outcome started being actively pursued.

achieved_at.title: Achieved At
achieved_at.description: When the change was judged to have happened.

achievement_note.title: Achievement Note
achievement_note.description: The basis on which this was judged achieved.

archived_at.title: Archived At
archived_at.description: When this outcome stopped being pursued.

archived_reason.title: Archived Reason
archived_reason.description: Why this outcome stopped being pursued. Shared vocabulary with Fast Flow Toolkit.

check_ins.title: Check-ins
check_ins.description: Dated observations about this outcome, kept with it.

supersedes.title: Supersedes
supersedes.description: An outcome this one replaces. The superseded outcome stays in the document.

decisionOption.title: Decision Option
decisionOption.description: OIO 1.1. One course of action that was considered. Listing an option asserts nothing about whether it was chosen — see flow_decision_record.chosen_option.

trade_offs.title: Trade-offs
trade_offs.description: What this option costs or gives up, and what would have to be true for it to work.

status.title: Option Status
status.description: How this option was treated. under-consideration: still live; rejected: ruled out; deferred: kept for later. An option with no status is simply one that was recorded.

flowDecisionRecord.title: Flow Decision Record
flowDecisionRecord.description: OIO 1.1. A decision being considered or made. Four independent axes are kept apart: status is where the decision stands as a decision, phase is where it sits on a roadmap, rollout_status is how far enactment has got, and verdict is what a later review concluded. A record with status 'draft' is a proposal and implies no approval, no commitment and no enactment.

id.title: FDR Id
id.description: Stable identifier for this decision record.

key.title: Key
key.description: A short human-facing reference (e.g. FDR-12), where the producing tool issues one.

question.title: Question
question.description: The question being decided, phrased as a question. Recording it keeps the record answerable later even if the chosen option is replaced.

context.title: Context
context.description: What was going on that made this decision necessary.

chosen_option.title: Chosen Option
chosen_option.description: The id of the option that was chosen, where one has been. Omit it while the decision is still open — an absent chosen option is the honest representation of an undecided decision.

decision.title: Decision
decision.description: What was decided, in a sentence. Required once status leaves draft; a draft record may carry a proposal in `options` and nothing here.

rationale.title: Rationale
rationale.description: Why this, given the evidence, the constraints and the alternatives.

expected_impact.title: Expected Impact
expected_impact.description: What is expected to change if this works, stated so a later review can tell whether it did.

next_steps.title: Next Steps
next_steps.description: What happens next to enact this.

intervention_type.title: Intervention Type
intervention_type.description: The kind of change this makes. Shared vocabulary with Fast Flow Toolkit.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: How confident the deciders are in this bet. This is about the decision, not about the evidence status of any signal cited.

reversibility.title: Reversibility
reversibility.description: How hard this would be to undo.

phase.title: Phase
phase.description: Where this sits on the roadmap. Shared vocabulary with Fast Flow Toolkit. Independent of status: a committed decision can still be scheduled 'later'.

status.title: Status
status.description: Where this stands as a decision. Shared vocabulary with Fast Flow Toolkit. draft: proposed, not committed; committed: decided; observing: enacted and being watched; reviewed: a verdict has been reached.

rollout_status.title: Rollout Status
rollout_status.description: How far enactment has actually got. Shared vocabulary with Fast Flow Toolkit. Deliberately separate from status: a decision can be committed and not yet started, or observing and only partly rolled out.

rollout_note.title: Rollout Note
rollout_note.description: What has and has not been enacted.

verdict.title: Verdict
verdict.description: What a review concluded about this decision as a bet. Shared vocabulary with Fast Flow Toolkit. The values are deliberately evidential rather than causal, because reviewing an organisational intervention against a window of check-ins yields evidence, not proof: supported: the evidence runs the way the bet predicted; not-supported: the evidence runs against it; inconclusive: not enough signal to judge. This is a judgement about the decision, and is not an Outcome: a decision can be enacted exactly as intended and be judged supported while the outcome it served has not moved.

review_horizon.title: Review Horizon
review_horizon.description: When this decision should be reviewed.

cites.title: Cites
cites.description: Signals offered as evidence for this decision. Citing a signal does not upgrade its evidence status.

serves.title: Serves
serves.description: The outcome this decision is intended to move. A decision serves at most one outcome; an outcome may be served by many decisions, which is the shape that says no single decision is sufficient.

affects.title: Affects
affects.description: Structural entities this decision touches, and how. This is intended effect, not structural dependency and not a sequence.

requires.title: Requires
requires.description: Other decisions that must land before this one can. This is decision ordering, not a process flow through the structural graph.

metrics.title: Metrics
metrics.description: Metrics this decision is tracked against.

check_ins.title: Check-ins
check_ins.description: Dated observations gathered while watching this decision, kept with it.

provenance.title: Provenance
provenance.description: Where this decision record came from.

supersedes.title: Supersedes
supersedes.description: A decision this one replaces. The superseded decision stays in the document with its own context, evidence and verdict intact.

supersede_note.title: Supersede Note
supersede_note.description: Why the earlier decision was replaced.

superseded_at.title: Superseded At
superseded_at.description: When this decision was superseded by another.

allOf.$comment: A decision that has left draft has been decided, so it must say what was decided.
A reviewed decision must carry the verdict that made it reviewed.

citesLink.title: Cites Link
citesLink.description: A decision citing a signal as evidence.

target.title: Signal
target.description: The id of the signal cited.

note.title: Note
note.description: What this signal contributed to the reasoning.

affectsLink.title: Affects Link
affectsLink.description: A structural entity a decision touches, and the part it plays.

target.title: Target
target.description: The id of the entity affected.

entity_type.title: Expected Entity Type
entity_type.description: Optional assertion about what kind of record the target is.

role.title: Role
role.description: Shared vocabulary with Fast Flow Toolkit. context: background to the decision; subject: what the decision is about; affected: touched by the consequences.
